description: Moves a webinar to another date, clock time, timezone or length without rebuilding it. For an evergreen webinar it changes the recurring times instead. Take it when the date moved. A host says: "We start two hours later, please move the whole thing." It needs the session and the webinar. For a live webinar you pass the date as YYYY-MM-DD, a clock time like 15:30, a timezone like Europe/Berlin and the length in minutes. For an evergreen one you pass the recurring blocks with time and weekdays. A bare hour with no am or pm is refused, never guessed. It writes on your site, the participant pages show the new date at once and the reminders move with it. The answer reads back the stored start and names every place the date shows. Side effect: it acts on your connected WordPress site; nothing else is touched. Words hosts use: move the date, change the time, new start, reschedule a webinar, timezone

duration_minutes.description: How long the webinar runs, in minutes (1-1440).

schedule.description: Evergreen only: {timezone, instant_access, blocks:[{time, weekdays}]} with up to three air-times.

session_id.description: From an earlier turn (weiter · texte · stand).

site.description: Which connected site is meant when this chat has more than one: the address exactly as wi_get_connector_status lists it under sites. Leave it out while only one site is connected.

start_date.description: The new live start date as YYYY-MM-DD. Leave it out for an evergreen webinar.

start_time.description: The new clock time, e.g. 15:30. A bare hour with no am/pm is refused as ambiguous.

start_timezone.description: The IANA timezone of that time, e.g. Europe/Berlin.

webinar_id.description: The webinar (campaign) id, as wi_list_webinars returned it. Never invent an id.

name: wi_change_webinar_schedule
title: Change when a webinar runs
